name: Frameleaf
description: A self-hosted photo and video library with native apps, private face and smart search, photo and video editing, and optional cloud backup. Beta; a fork of Immich.
longDescription:
Frameleaf is a photo and video library that runs on your own NAS, home server or Linux machine with Docker. Your originals stay as ordinary files on your own disks. Faces, smart search and AI captions are worked out on your own hardware, and there is no telemetry. It has native apps for iPhone, iPad, Android, Apple TV and Android TV, a desktop app for Mac, Windows and Linux, a photo editor, Studio (a video editor), Boards for references and design files, and client galleries for photographers.

Bring everything home: import a Google Photos Takeout, sync iCloud Photos, or add folders already on your disks. Search in plain words, find text in photos and words spoken in videos, and rediscover memories, places and landmarks. Give each person in the family their own library and share with partner sharing, albums and links. Library Care finds duplicates and missing or damaged originals.

The server is open source (AGPLv3) and a fork of Immich. Frameleaf is in beta. Frameleaf Cloud is optional and adds remote access, off-site backup, buddy backup and cloud GPU processing.

This template runs the Frameleaf server, the machine-learning service and the bundled PostgreSQL database. On first visit the web UI asks you to create the admin account. Recommended: 6 GB RAM and 2 CPU cores. Docs: frameleaf.app/docs.
